topology: VLAN 10 has two SLAAC PCs on SW1 Gi0/1–2, legitimate advertiser R1 2001:db8:10::1/64 and fe80::1 on Gi0/3, and live ROGUE 2001:db8:bad::1/64 and fe80::bad on Gi0/4. R1 Gi0/1 connects to remote HTTP/ping SRV1 2001:db8:20::10/64 with a prepared return route. ROGUE keeps advertising while the lab is protected.
verificationNotes: Practice begins with zero credit despite actual automatically learned legitimate and rogue addresses and an unwanted gateway. Published IOS commands earn five policy tasks. Real delivered RA/DAD traffic earns live client, gateway and neighbor goals; two actual remote IPv6 pings complete all twelve tasks.

HOST-PORTS uses device-role host on the two client ports and rogue ingress. ROUTER-PORT uses device-role router only toward R1. Neither policy is trusted and no extra source/prefix/flag restrictions are required. Definitions without attachments, router role on rogue ingress and trusted-port bypass are tested as failures.

Dropped RA proof correlates actual ingress, rogue link-local address/MAC, prefix, packet ID and ICMPv6 type 134. Bounded 1000-row telemetry and packet metadata expose the advertisement to the existing packet inspector. Counters, unrelated drops and disconnected sources cannot fabricate the observation.

Reset and request IPv6 is an explicit NetworkSim adapter control, not Windows CLI syntax. It removes only owned automatic IPv6 addresses/routes and pending DAD/configuration, then sends a real RS. Manual IPv6/IPv4 addresses and manual routes remain. Repeated resets, invalid interfaces and poisoned-state recovery are tested.

Blocking new RAs does not erase earlier learned prefixes. Removing the rogue host attachment admits real unwanted RAs and poisons clients; restoring the policy plus resetting automatic state repairs them. Host role on the legitimate uplink blocks fresh SLAAC until corrected; restrictive prefix checks and trusted bypass are also exercised.

Client proof requires a current owned SLAAC address/lease, valid legitimate advertised default router and absence of the rogue prefix. Neighbor goals require the actual link-local MAC and received NDP reply. Routed-ping goals correlate requests and replies from those real client addresses. RA lifetime expiry invalidates live gateway proof even while an address remains.

The existing RA policy show path now uses Cisco-style configuration and attachment lines, retaining actual VLAN attachment inventory. Removing a guard policy field deletes its configuration instead of storing undefined values, so saved and running policy objects round-trip consistently.

Saved observations retain achieved rogue-drop and routed-ping tasks. Live SLAAC, gateway and neighbor state rebuild through actual traffic after reopening. The completed reference includes only five configuration goals before the engine observes traffic; no runtime evidence is fabricated.
